---
title: "Quiz: the level set equation"
---

Short questions to test your understanding. Try each on paper first, then open the answer. Convention: $\phi < 0$ inside, $F > 0$ moves the curve outward, $\phi_t + F|\nabla\phi| = 0$.

---

**Q1.** At a pixel, $|\nabla\phi| = 2$ and $F = 1$. By how much does $\phi$ change in a time step $\Delta t = 0.1$? Does it go up or down?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
$\phi^{n+1} = \phi^n - \Delta t\,F\,|\nabla\phi|$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Down by $0.1 \cdot 1 \cdot 2 = 0.2$. A steep $\phi$ must change more to move its zero crossing by the same distance $F\Delta t = 0.1$.
:::

---

**Q2.** Why does a velocity **along** the curve not appear in the level set equation?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
What happens to the curve if every point slides along it?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Sliding points along the curve leaves the curve (the set of points) unchanged; only the motion across it changes the shape. In the derivation it shows up as $\nabla\phi\cdot\mathbf v = 0$ for a tangential $\mathbf v$.
:::

---

**Q3.** A front grows ($F > 0$). At a pixel, the left neighbour has a smaller $\phi$ and the right neighbour a larger one. Which difference does the upwind scheme use in $x$?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
From which side does a growing front arrive?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
The backward difference $\phi_i - \phi_{i-1}$: a growing front comes from the inside, the side of smaller $\phi$, here the left.
:::

---

**Q4.** Why does a shrinking interval never disappear when $|\nabla\phi|$ is computed with central differences?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Compute the central difference at the bottom of $|x| - 1$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
At the minimum the two neighbours are equal, so the central difference is 0: $\phi$ there never changes and stays negative. The upwind scheme for a shrinking front uses both one-sided slopes at the minimum (the front arrives from both sides) and raises the value.
:::

---

**Q5.** $F = 2$ pixels per unit time on a 2D grid with $\Delta x = 1$. What is the largest stable time step? And in 1D?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
At most one pixel per step; a diagonal front counts in both directions.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
2D: $\Delta t \le 1/(\sqrt2 \cdot 2) = 0.35$. 1D: $\Delta t \le 1/2 = 0.5$.
:::

---

**Q6.** A circle of radius 20 moves under curvature flow with $\varepsilon = 1$. When does it vanish? What is its radius halfway through that time?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
$r(t)^2 = r_0^2 - 2t$.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
It vanishes at $t = 400/2 = 200$. At $t = 100$: $r = \sqrt{400 - 200} = 14.1$. It shrinks slowly at first and fast at the end, because small circles have large curvature.
:::

---

**Q7.** A dumbbell (two disks joined by a thin bar) moves with constant speed $F = -1$, and separately under pure curvature flow. In which case does it split in two?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
What is the sign of $\kappa$ on the sides of the bar, near the disks?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
With constant inward speed: the bar disappears after a time equal to half its thickness, and the shape splits. Under curvature flow it does **not** split: the concave corners where bar meets disk have $\kappa < 0$ and move outward, the neck widens, and the curve becomes convex and shrinks to a point as one piece (Grayson's theorem).
:::

---

**Q8.** Why reinitialise $\phi$, if the zero contour is all we want?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
What do the derivatives of $\phi$ look like after many steps?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
After many steps $\phi$ becomes very steep in some places and flat in others. Finite differences of a very steep or very flat $\phi$ are inaccurate (curvature especially), the time-step rule assumes $|\nabla\phi| \approx 1$, and a flat $\phi$ near the front can let noise flip signs. Resetting $\phi$ to the signed distance of its own zero contour fixes the values without moving the curve.
:::

---

**Q9.** *(math)* For curvature flow with $\varepsilon = 1$, show that the area inside any simple closed curve decreases at the rate $2\pi$.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
$A' = -\oint F\,ds$, and the total turning of a simple closed curve.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Each piece $ds$ of the curve moves outward by $F\,dt$, sweeping area $F\,ds\,dt$, so $A' = \oint F\,ds = -\oint\kappa\,ds$. The tangent of a simple closed curve turns once around: $\oint\kappa\,ds = 2\pi$. Hence $A' = -2\pi$, whatever the shape.
:::
